T07.1.title: Rename on title edit, and move between folders
T07.1.what:
Pure TypeScript over the `Host` interface: renaming a note when its title changes, and moving a note to another folder. No UI, no Rust, no new dependencies. Part of #24 (T07).

## Brief

**Where:** new module `src/core/notes/rename.ts`, tests in `src/core/notes/rename.test.ts` (Vitest, on `MemoryHost` from `src/host/memory-host.ts`). Use `fileNameFor` from `src/core/file-name/file-name.ts` and `saveNote`/`loadNote` from `src/core/notes/repository.ts`. Keep it in its own file so it does not collide with other work on `repository.ts`.

**Behavior:**
1. `renameNote(host, path, note, newTitle)`: save the note with the new title in its header first (through `saveNote`, so the save guard still applies), then move the file to `fileNameFor(newTitle, names in the folder except this file)`. Return the new path.
2. A change that only differs in capital letters ("note" to "Note") still renames the file. `host.move` already allows that case.
3. A clash with another file gets " 2", " 3" (that is what `fileNameFor` does).
4. If the move fails, the title stays saved in the header, the file keeps its old name, and the result says so with a short notice (for example `{ path, renamed: false, notice }`). Never lose the title edit.
5. `moveNote(host, path, folder)`: move the file into another folder, keeping its name, or the next free name if one is taken there. `noteId` and content never change.
6. Refuse a destination inside `.vaultops/` (`isInsideVaultOps`) and a note that is read-only from the scan. Write nothing in those cases.

**Out of scope:** UI, duplicate `noteId` handling (T07.2), folder operations (T18), Rust.

**Tests:** rename keeps `noteId` and blocks; capital-letter-only rename changes the file name; clash gets " 2"; a host whose `move` fails leaves the old file name and a header with the new title, and reports it; move to another folder, including a name clash there; destinations inside `.vaultops/` are refused with no writes.
done: Rename and move keep `noteId` and content
A capital-letter-only title change still renames the file
A rename into an existing name gets " 2"
A failed rename keeps the new title in the header and the old file name, and reports it
`npm run check` passes
T07.1.note: On the real Mac file system the capital-letter-only rename is checked later by the Mac test button; the fake host already behaves like the Mac.

T07.2.title: Duplicate noteId warning and "give this copy a new id"
T07.2.what:
Pure TypeScript over the `Host` interface: the action behind "give this copy a new id" for two files with the same `noteId` (for example a copy made in Finder). No UI, no Rust, no new dependencies. Part of #24 (T07).

## Brief

**Where:** new module `src/core/notes/duplicate-id.ts`, tests in `src/core/notes/duplicate-id.test.ts` (Vitest, on `MemoryHost`). Detection already exists: `scanVault` in `src/core/notes/scan.ts` fills `duplicateOf` and marks both copies read-only. Reuse it; do not change how scan reports duplicates.

**Behavior:**
1. `giveNewId(host, path)`: load the note, check (by scanning or by an argument the caller passes from a scan) that its `noteId` really is used by another file, then save it with a fresh `crypto.randomUUID()` as `noteId`. Only the header's `noteId` changes; title, props and every block stay byte-for-byte the same when written back.
2. Refuse, writing nothing, when the note is not a duplicate, when it is damaged, truncated or from a newer format (only notes that read cleanly can be rewritten), or when the path is inside `.vaultops/`.
3. Never run automatically: nothing calls it except the user's action (UI comes later).
4. After the action, a new scan shows no duplicate for either file, and both are no longer read-only.

**Out of scope:** UI, rename and move (T07.1), Rust.

**Tests:** two copies with the same id: the action changes only the chosen file's `noteId`, the other file is untouched; the rest of the chosen file's text is unchanged; refused for a non-duplicate, a truncated copy and a newer-format copy; a rescan reports no duplicates.
done: Duplicates are found on scan (already built; covered again here)
The action changes only the chosen file's `noteId`
It refuses damaged, truncated and newer-format notes and writes nothing
`npm run check` passes

T08.2.title: Delete to trash and restore
T08.2.what:
Pure TypeScript over the `Host` interface: moving a note to the vault's Trash and putting it back, using the layout decided in T08.1. Uses `host.move` only: nothing is erased. Delete forever is T08.3. No UI, no Rust, no new dependencies. Part of #27 (T08).

## Brief

**Where:** new module `src/core/notes/trash.ts`, tests in `src/core/notes/trash.test.ts` (Vitest, on `MemoryHost`).

**Layout (decided in T08.1):** a deleted note moves to `.vaultops/trash/<timestamp>/<original relative path>`. The timestamp is UTC with no colons, for example `2026-10-27T15-04-05-123Z`; if that folder already exists, add " 2", " 3". No separate record file.

**Behavior:**
1. `trashNote(host, path)`: create the folders it needs (`host.makeFolder`), then `host.move` the note there. Refuse paths inside `.vaultops/`.
2. `listTrash(host)`: every trashed note with its original path and deletion time, read from the folder layout, newest first.
3. `restoreNote(host, trashPath)`: move it back to its original path. If the original folder no longer exists, restore to the vault root. If the name is taken, use the next free name with " 2" (compared the way `fileNameFor` compares: capital letters and Unicode form count as the same). Remove the timestamp folder once it is empty only if `Host` can already do that; otherwise leave it (T08.3 adds removal).
4. Nothing here ever erases a file. Trash is never emptied automatically.

**Out of scope:** delete forever (T08.3), the Trash screen and its confirmation (T24.1), Rust.

**Tests:** delete then restore gives the same text at the same path; restore when the folder is gone goes to the root; restore with a name clash and with a capital-letter-only clash gets " 2"; two deletes in the same millisecond do not collide; deleting from inside `.vaultops/` is refused; `listTrash` shows original paths and times.
done: Delete, restore, restore into a missing folder (vault root), restore with a name clash (" 2", including a capital-letter-only clash)
No code path erases a note
`npm run check` passes

#135.title: Recover interrupted vault creation when config.json is missing
#135.what:
An interrupted creation leaves `.vaultops/` present but `config.json` missing, and the folder stays damaged forever.

Update `src/core/vault/vault.ts` to recognize an unfinished creation containing only empty reserved folders and safely finish creating the vault. Preserve existing data and keep genuinely damaged or populated vaults protected.
done: Missing config plus only empty reserved folders can finish creation
A populated or unexpected entry is not overwritten or mistaken for an unfinished creation
Regression tests added and `npm run check` passes
